item.title: Foster carers push for counselling support as minister confirms extra foster leave
item.description: Foster carers told a Foundation for Social Welfare Services conference on adverse childhood experiences that they were initially reluctant to accept therapy suggested by their social workers, with one carer saying threats from biological family members were the breaking point that made them question whether to continue. Alternative Care Directorate director Melissa Gauci said children entering foster care often bring experiences of neglect and trauma that do not disappear even in a safe environment. Social Policy Minister Michael Falzon referred to a 2027 Budget measure under which people who begin fostering a child next year will be entitled to an additional 10 working days of government-funded leave. Ministry figures cited put the number of children living with foster families at 217, of whom 118 are in permanent alternative care and 25 are young adults over 18 still residing with their carers.

item.title: Two cars collide at the Kappara junction; police confirm nobody was injured
item.description: Two cars were involved in an accident at the Kappara junction on Triq Mikiel Anton Vassalli. Police confirmed that nobody was hurt in the incident. An ambulance was also dispatched to the scene, both as a precaution and as part of normal procedure, a police spokesman said.

item.title: SMEs call for urgent talks over proposed foreign student fee hikes
item.description: The Malta Chamber of SMEs has called for an urgent meeting with government to reassess proposed steep fee increases for non-EU students, warning they could undermine Maltas competitiveness as an education hub. Bill 15, implementing the Budget 2027 measures, would triple some visa fees, raising long-stay study visa fees from 100 to 300 and from 150 to 400 for extended service, while the initial study permit fee would rise tenfold from 50 to 500 alongside an annual 400 infrastructure contribution. The Chamber said the measures were introduced without prior consultation and risk diverting prospective students to competing countries.

item.title: Government considers legal action over stalled Marsalforn garden works
item.description: Gozo Minister Clint Camilleri told parliament that the contractor selected to embellish the nien it-Tliet Għoljiet garden in Marsalforn breached its contractual obligations, leaving the long-awaited project at a standstill. The ministry is taking all necessary measures, including judicial action, to ensure the contractor honours its commitments, with work so far limited to the removal of old material and no expenditure incurred on the project so far. The admission comes three years after the government first pledged to upgrade the garden, which has been repeatedly delayed since.

item.title: Court bars Bernice Cilias murderer husband from inheriting her estate
item.description: The Civil Court declared Roderick Cassar, who admitted murdering his wife Bernice Cilia in 2022 and is serving 40 years in prison, legally unworthy of inheriting from her. Cilia died without leaving a will, so under normal rules half her estate would have passed to her husband and half to their two children, aged 11 and eight. Her parents, acting for the children, petitioned the court under Articles 605 and 796 of the Civil Code, and Cassar admitted their claims in a note to the court on November 10. Madam Justice Joanne Vella Cuschieri upheld the application, ordering the entire estate to pass to the children and Cassar to pay the costs of the proceedings.

item.title: National Archives renews call for purpose-built facility after years of delays
item.description: The National Archives has made securing a purpose-built facility a key priority in its Strategic Vision 2035, unveiled last week alongside a new institutional identity, citing unsuitable buildings, limited storage capacity and environmental risks for the nations records. The call comes years after plans for a new archives complex at Ta Qali were abandoned, with the site instead used for the concert venue. Other priorities include strengthening digitisation, preserving digital records and improving access to research and educational resources.

item.title: Over 400 object to planned 28-warehouse complex outside Luqa development zone
item.description: More than 400 people have objected to an application to demolish a disused farm and build a 28-warehouse complex outside the development zone in Luqa, in the same area where a similar application was refused five years ago. The plan, application PA/00750/23, covers 14,000 square metres at Triq il-Qasam Sperimentali and Triq San Vincenz De Paola in the &Ħal Farruġ area, with around 4,420 square metres of floor space, parking and 58 new trees. Planning Authority officers are recommending approval, in contrast to the refusal of an earlier application on the same site.

item.title: Culture minister backtracks, pledges to regain artists trust but will not resign
item.description: Culture Minister Malcolm Paul Agius Galea said he takes responsibility for the reaction his remarks provoked and pledged to work to regain the artistic communitys trust, after a meeting with the president of the Malta Entertainment Industry and Arts Association (MEIA). His remarks at the Festival of Ideas describing his first months in office as traumatic, saying some artists consider themselves Gods gift to the world and that creativity should follow certain norms triggered a petition by 56 organisations and 3,327 creative professionals calling for his resignation. The minister acknowledged aspects of his speech could have been expressed better, stopped short of an outright apology, and said he is not resigning, announcing a work plan of individual meetings with artists and visits to their workplaces.

item.title: PNs Darren Carabott keeps options open on deputy leader race
item.description: Nationalist Party economy spokesperson and MP Darren Carabott declined to say whether he will contest one of the two deputy leader roles, saying such decisions should be settled inside the party first. The PN is changing its statute to revive two deputy leader posts, one for party affairs and one for parliamentary affairs, with Alex Perici Calascione currently holding the single role. Incumbent Perici Calascione and MP Mark Anthony Sammut have both publicly declared their interest and informed PN leader Alex Borg.

item.title: Hostels warn €8 tourist tax could wipe out Maltas backpacker market
item.description: A group of nine licensed hostels have warned that the increased eco-contribution could wipe out Maltas backpacker niche market and threaten the survival of independent operators. They called for a tiered system based on accommodation category, saying the flat €8 fee could force several hostels to close their doors. They said they are not asking for visitors to be exempt from contributing to Maltas environmental and tourism sustainability objectives but for a fairer and more proportionate approach, noting that most European destinations charge lower rates for budget accommodation.

item.title: Government to publish document on tenants rights and obligations
item.description: The government will prepare a document setting out the rights and obligations of those entering a rental contract, complementing the Buyers Charter. The initiative follows a public consultation on the Buyers Charter that drew 33 submissions, with feedback that people living in rented property also need clarity on their rights and responsibilities. Accommodation and Arts Minister Owen Bonnici made the announcement at a meeting with property-sector professionals organised by the Housing Authority, saying both initiatives are part of government work to improve transparency, certainty and trust in the sector.

item.title: Traditional Maltese mazzit joins ġbejna on EU protected foods list
item.description: The European Commission has approved the registration of traditional Maltese blood pudding mazzit as a Protected Geographical Indication in a regulation published on Friday. The listing places mazzit in the EUs eAmbrosia register of geographical indications, joining thousands of protected European products, with only producers meeting specific requirements able to use the protected name. The recognition follows a years-long effort led by the Public Abattoir to revive a product authorities say was at risk of disappearing, and comes less than two years after ġbejna received EU protection.

item.title: Court rules deportation of father of two young children disproportionate
item.description: A court has ruled that the deportation of a father of two young children was disproportionate because immigration authorities failed to consider the impact on his family. Balwinder Singh, 39, was convicted in August of presenting forged architect documents falsely stating that five people could live in a property instead of three, and received a four-month suspended sentence. A principal immigration officer then issued the deportation order; Singh challenged it before the Immigration Appeals Board while in detention, and the board upheld his appeal and ordered his release.

item.title: Widow sues care home over husbands death after alleged assault by resident
item.description: A widow has filed a civil lawsuit against the operators of a Fgura care home after her husband died following an alleged assault by his roommate. Antonia Perini is seeking damages over the death of Giuseppe Perini, who was attacked at Dar San Ġużepp on 14 October 2025 and died at Mater Dei Hospital two weeks later after suffering serious injuries. She claims the attack was carried out by a fellow resident in the same room who allegedly had a history of behavioural problems associated with severe dementia.

item.title: Animal care clinic to get €700,000 more next year, reaching €1.35 million
item.description: Funding for the animal care clinic will increase by €700,000 next year, taking its total allocation to €1.35 million under Budget 2027. Parliamentary Secretary for Animal Welfare Alicia Bugeja Said said three support schemes for voluntary organisations and sanctuaries will also be relaunched: the Free Veterinary Services Scheme, the Maintenance of Animal Sanctuaries Scheme and the Animal Welfare Fund. She said the additional funding would strengthen animal care services and support organisations that dedicate themselves to the work.

item.title: Over 6,000 people helped by Victim Support Agency in five years
item.description: More than 6,000 people have received assistance from the Victim Support Agency since it was established five years ago. The agencys panic alarm service was used by 125 people in the first ten months of this year, against 84 across the whole of 2025. Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield said a common referral system would be strengthened so that victims are directed to the services they need without having to repeatedly recount their traumatic experiences, linking victim protection directly to crime prevention.

item.title: Gozo-Sicily agreement aims to open new markets for Gozitan producers
item.description: Gozo and Sicily have signed a memorandum of understanding expected to create new opportunities for Gozitan farmers, fishermen and businesses. The agreement, signed between CNA Sicilia and the Gozo Confederation for Agriculture and Fisheries during the Taormina Food Expo, will facilitate exports, the promotion of Gozitan products and collaboration between businesses on the two islands. Gozo Minister Clint Camilleri said it could lead to joint Mediterranean brands capable of competing in international markets.

item.title: Medservs nine-month EBITDA climbs 8.5% to €17.8 million
item.description: MedservRegis published an interim report showing revenue up 30% to €89.1 million for the first nine months of 2026, with EBITDA advancing 8.5% to €17.8 million. The company said it expects full-year 2026 results to remain ahead of the forecasts in its updated Financial Analysis Summary dated 19 June 2026, which projected revenue of €99.8 million and EBITDA of €21.9 million. The results were published after the close of trading, in a session when the MSE Equity Price Index edged up 0.26% to 4,307.3 points.

item.title: Scientists discover 200m seabed bulge linked to fault system shaping Malta and Gozo
item.description: Scientists have identified a massive underwater bulge rising 200m above the surrounding seabed between Malta and the Italian island of Pantelleria. The structure stretches 26km in length and 4.6km in width at depths between 1,400m and 1,750m in the northern sector of the Malta Graben, lying 60km to 80km west-northwest of Malta. The findings were published in the journal Tectonophysics in a study led by Nicolò Chizzini of Italys National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology.

item.title: MPT investigates clash between passenger and bus inspector caught on camera
item.description: Malta Public Transport is investigating an altercation between a bus inspector and a passenger caught on camera on Friday morning. Footage shared on social media shows the passenger pushing the inspector on the Route 82B bus towards Birżebbuġa, with the inspector then grabbing the passenger by the neck, while another passenger is heard asking whether he can buy the man a €2 ticket. The dispute appears to have arisen over an unpaid bus ticket; the company said it has zero tolerance for violence.

item.title: Marc Alden to step down as Deloitte Malta CEO in June 2027
item.description: Marc Alden will step down as chief executive of Deloitte Malta in June 2027, closing a leadership tenure spanning two terms. Alden joined the firm in 1994 and has led it as CEO since January 2020, meaning that by then he will have served the maximum two terms permitted under the firms governance rules. He will remain with Deloitte Malta as a partner taking on the role of Government and Public Sector Business Leader, and said he looked forward to working more closely with government as Malta enters an important period of transformation.

item.title: Winners of Maltas oldest architectural and conservation awards announced
item.description: A converted guesthouse in Senglea with a contemporary rooftop extension was the overall winner of the 20th edition of the Din l-Art Ħelwa Architectural Heritage Awards. Stilla San Mikiel, the second property in an albergo diffuso spread across the Three Cities, was designed by Valentino Architects and received the Judge Maurice Caruana Curran Award, also sharing the Rehabilitation and Re-use of Buildings Award with Elementi, a wellness and hospitality project in Mosta. A public garden in the former oil storage depot in Birgu was among the other winners.

item.title: ADPD: cycling strategy needs road space taken from cars, not just promises
item.description: ADPD welcomed the National Cycling Strategy 2026-2036 launched on Wednesday but warned it will achieve little unless the government takes road space away from private cars. The Green Party said the strategy sets out a nationwide network of routes linking homes, schools, workplaces and transport hubs, but stops short of implementation budgets and deadlines, with the route network still to be mapped out. Party spokesperson Mario Mallia said awareness campaigns alone will not make cycling a realistic alternative to the car.

item.title: Police chief says court expert is stalling the Daphne murder leaks inquiry
item.description: Police Commissioner Angelo Gafà said an investigation into information leaks from the Daphne Caruana Galizia murder case has been held up by an unnamed court-appointed expert who was assigned to examine data from a suspects mobile phone in 2021 and has still not carried out the work. Speaking to Andrew Azzopardi on Campus FM, the commissioner said police have charged several people but keep reaching a standstill while awaiting the experts findings. Gafà said he was disappointed at the criticism levelled at the police over the delay.

item.title: Malta HR Survey finds hiring and retention are employers top challenge
item.description: The Malta HR Survey 2026 by the Foundation for Human Resources Development found that 72% of respondents cited hiring challenges as their most pressing people issue, followed by leadership capability at 45% and pay competitiveness at 43%. Asked about the next two to three years, respondents shifted to retention at 58% and attracting scarce skills at 53%, with 39% flagging leadership pipelines and succession planning. The findings were presented at Maltas Annual HR Conference and Expo, held in October under the theme HR Lead: Powering Strategy Through People.

item.title: Abela hails EU agreement on Ukraine peace talks as glimmer of hope
item.description: Prime Minister Robert Abela welcomed an agreement among European leaders, reached at an informal summit in Dublin, on how Europe will be represented in future peace talks between Russia and Ukraine. Under the deal, Germany, France, the United Kingdom, Italy and Poland the E5 together with the European Commission and European Council will negotiate on Europes behalf. Abela called the development a glimmer of hope, noting Malta has consistently advocated a peaceful solution since the conflict began.

item.title: Scope Ratings affirms Maltas A+ credit rating with a stable outlook
item.description: The Labour Party has welcomed the international credit rating agencys decision to affirm Maltas A+ rating with a stable outlook, calling it a vote of confidence in the management of public finances. Scope forecasts the Maltese economy will grow by 4.1% this year and continue to outperform other eurozone economies, and notes that the governments policy of keeping energy prices stable has largely shielded household bills. Malta recorded the second-highest economic growth rate in the EU in 2025.

item.title: Saint James Hospital broadcasts weight-loss procedure live to MedTech conference
item.description: Saint James Hospital transmitted a combined weight-loss procedure live to international medical specialists attending the MedTech World Europe 2026 conference in Valletta, the first time the hospital has done so. Performed by Prof. Christina Stier with Dr Andrea Formiga, it combined Endoscopic Sleeve Gastroplasty, which reduces stomach capacity by about 70 per cent, with Gastric Mucosal Ablation to treat the stomach lining. Hospital CEO Jean Claude Muscat said the event showcased Maltese medical staff on the international stage.

item.title: Floriana horse death: no signs of neglect or overexertion found
item.description: The Animal Welfare Directorate said an external examination of the horse that collapsed and died while pulling a karozzin in Floriana on Wednesday found no apparent signs of abuse, neglect or overexertion. The incident happened on St Francis Street hill, where the horse was pulling a carriage carrying two tourists downhill. The directorate confirmed the finding on Saturday and said it will assess whether any further action is warranted.

item.title: Five schools build online training for educators under 60,000 EU project
item.description: Three Maltese schools and two from Slovenia and Slovakia are taking part in an Erasmus+ project led by St Francis School in Birkirkara to develop online training resources for early childhood educators. The 60,000 initiative focuses on the emergent curriculum, with participants observing teaching methods abroad, exchanging practice through job shadowing and receiving training videos. Minister for European Funds Keith Azzopardi Tanti addressed the launch event, saying the resources will be usable beyond the participating schools.

item.title: Man wanted by a magistrate found within hours of police notice
item.description: A man wanted by a magistrate in connection with an ongoing court case was found within hours of the police issuing a public notice about him on Saturday. Police published a photograph of Jean Paul Chetcuti and appealed to the public for help in tracking him down, and later confirmed the man had been located.

item.title: Din l-Art Ħelwa serves judicial letter seeking Grade 1 protection for Fort Chambray barracks
item.description: The heritage NGO has asked the Planning Authority and the Superintendence of Cultural Heritage to schedule the British Barracks at Fort Chambray, Għajnsielem, and their surroundings as Grade 1 protected sites. The NGO says its April 2024 application is still undecided more than two years on, and that the October 2026 master-plan amendment preserving the barracks is not a substitute for statutory protection. The barracks were named among Europa Nostras most endangered heritage sites.

item.title: Malta Rescue Corps unveils new equipment for safer patient transport
item.description: A Malta Rescue Corps project has been inaugurated to strengthen the transport and assistance the organisation offers to people with disabilities, people with limited mobility and those in vulnerable situations. The equipment was financed through the Quality of Life Small Grants Scheme 2026 and includes ambulance stretchers, patient transport chairs, portable wheelchair ramps, vital-signs monitoring devices and a defibrillator, aimed at helping volunteers move patients more safely and accessibly.

item.title: Malta records the EUs largest quarterly rise in greenhouse gas emissions
item.description: Maltas seasonally adjusted greenhouse gas emissions rose by an estimated 4.8% in the second quarter of 2026 compared with the first quarter, the largest increase among EU countries, according to Eurostat figures. Malta was one of only eight member states to record an increase over the April to June period, as the EU works towards cutting its overall emissions.

item.title: Heritage watchdog conditionally accepts Bormla reservoir demolition for 104-space car park
item.description: Transport Maltas plan to demolish the historic Bormla reservoir outside St Helens Gate and rebuild it beneath a 104-space car park has received conditional approval from the Superintendence of Cultural Heritage. The watchdog said planning application PA/06799/26 could be considered provided the parking stays within the reservoirs existing footprint, to safeguard the nearby Grade 1 scheduled fortifications, and asked for clearer drawings. The scheme faces objections from the Stormwater Directorate and the environmental NGO Flimkien għal Ambjent Aħjar.

item.title: MCAST part-time lecturers left unpaid as union dispute drags on
item.description: Part-time lecturers at MCAST have gone without their October salaries as an industrial dispute over administrative and support staff spills over into teaching staff. The UĦM is negotiating a new collective agreement with the college, and its directives telling administrative staff not to answer calls or e-mails, or to process payment claims, have blocked lecturers pay. Full-time lecturers have received regular salaries but are still owed overtime, with lecturers warning the dispute could leave them without pay for months.

item.title: Doctors say Maltas diabetes problem is worse than figures suggest
item.description: Diabetes specialists said official figures around 10% of the population diagnosed, one of the highest rates in Europe understate the true scale of the condition, with many more people likely living with undiagnosed diabetes. Prof. David Coppini and Dr Sandro Vella, speaking at a national conference at San Anton Palace, called for a national diabetes register to track every patient and understand who is affected. Parents who repeatedly took their children to doctors before diagnosis raised concerns about missed warning signs at a Maltese Diabetes Association seminar marking World Diabetes Day, where the absence of a national screening programme was again raised.
